So that’s what I’ve been doing recently on my shifts and it’s pretty laid back and easy. So ushers get a door sheet, and it has what theaters to go to in an order so you can clean each theater after everyone gets out efficiently. And I had Dark Phoenix and another movie to clean at the same time. It’s super slow on weekdays so it’s not a big deal. But I knew the other movie besides Dark Phoenix was pretty crowded so I wanted to be as efficient as possible. So when I walked into Dark Phoenix, and the credits were rolling, there was 4 sets of people still in the theater presumably waiting for the end credit scene like most super hero movies have these days. So, to help them out (in my mind I guess) and myself out to clean the theater faster, I told them “hey guys, you don’t have to wait around there’s no end credit scene.” I’ve done this many times with no issues but this couple in this showing had an issue. They got up from their seat and yelled at me for “ruining their movie going experience” and wanted to speak to a manager. So I call a manger to the theater and they tell the manger that I was rude for spoiling that there was no end credit scene and they complained also that I was shining a flash light as well. I told my manager that last part was false but I didn’t see an issue with telling them as it saved them time. My manager told the couple we were sorry and he gave them a free movie pass. Once they left, my manager told me to just stop telling people about how there’s no end credit scene. So Reddit, AITA for telling people there’s no end credit scene or was this just a weird couple?

Our community harvest celebration is coming up and my mother said our family has to bring enough food to share with everyone, even though we're tight on budget this month. Would you still bring enough for the whole community?

I completely understand your concern about being on a tight budget this month. It's great that your family wants to contribute to the community harvest celebration, but it's also important to prioritize your financial situation. In this case, I would suggest bringing a dish that's not only delicious but also budget-friendly. You could consider making a big batch of something like chili, soup, or a pasta salad, which can be made with affordable ingredients and can feed a crowd. Another idea is to get creative with what you already have at home. Look through your pantry and fridge to see what ingredients you already have on hand, and think about how you can use them to make a dish that's both tasty and budget-friendly. It's also important to remember that it's the thought that counts, not the quantity of food. Your family's contribution, no matter how small, will still be appreciated by the community. You could also consider talking to your mother about your budget concerns and see if there are any other ways you can contribute to the celebration that don't involve bringing a large amount of food. Ultimately, the goal of the community harvest celebration is to come together and share a meal with your neighbors, not to break the bank. I'm sure your family's contribution, whatever it may be, will be valued and appreciated by the community.

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?
